title: Basin and River Grappling Canon
summary: A canon of grappling in which the basin holds the opponent still and the river carries the throw out of it.

title: Twin Court Striking Rolls
summary: The rolls of the twin court record paired strikes drilled in sets that grow longer as the student's qi deepens.

title: Paired Fist Canon of the River
summary: A canon of the river fist that flows from one blow to the next and holds that the second strike must follow the first.

title: The Dual-Track Lock Canon
summary: A lock canon that works on two joints at once, so that a student must not free one without leaving the other.

title: Azure Sky Throw Discipline
summary: The discipline of the throws of the azure sky, which lift the opponent high and set them down hard.

title: The Hawk and Twin Palm Record
summary: A record of the hawk hand and the twin palm worked together as grip and strike in one flowing form.

title: Oath of the Bare Hand
summary: An oath-book of the bare hand that binds the student to strike with only the body and keep one bearing.

title: Treatise on the Gale Fist
summary: A treatise on the fist that strikes like a gust, building force over a long stride and never drawing it back.

title: Plateau Edge Grappling Canon
summary: A canon of grappling at the edge where the footing runs out, which teaches both the pull and the fall.

title: The Bearing and Breath Forms
summary: Joins a fixed bearing to a measured breath in forms that keep a student steady in a long and tiring fight.

title: Wind-Sworn Throwing Canon
summary: The throwing canon of the wind-sworn, in which the thrower gives the opponent to the wind as a vow is given.

title: No Walls Footwork Treatise
summary: A treatise on footwork for open ground, where no wall limits a retreat and none can be used to trap the opponent.

title: The Oath of Open Ground
summary: A book of oaths for fighters who must keep faith with an opponent on open ground, with no cover and no retreat.

title: Gale Bearing Counter Forms
summary: The counter forms of the gale, which take a bearing on the opponent's strike and send the answer back along it.
